info.title: test-cap /auth routes
info.description: The routes `auth.handle` serves. Internal use only. Every `POST` needs the app's `Origin` and the synchronizer token from `GET /auth/session`, sent as the `X-CSRF-Token` header or a `csrfToken` field. Every reply carries `Cache-Control: no-store` and the security headers. Generated from the dispatcher's route table.

csrfHeader.name: X-CSRF-Token
csrfHeader.description: The synchronizer token. A `POST` may send it as the `csrfToken` body field instead, never both.

get.summary: Read the session and get a CSRF token
get.description: Returns the request's session, or `null`, and a synchronizer token for the next `POST`. A browser with no cookie gets a pre-session cookie the token is bound to.

post.summary: Confirm the address with the emailed code
post.description: Redeems the 6-digit code sign-up mailed, once, within 24 hours, and claims the address for the `pre-auth` session's account. The reply is the same when another account already confirmed the address; then nothing is claimed. Each attempt counts, over the code's whole life: after 5 the code dies, and further attempts answer 429 until a resend issues a new code. Confirming adds no assurance.

post.summary: Make a new set of recovery codes
post.description: Makes 10 saved recovery codes. Each is shown once and stored only as an argon2id hash, and the old set stops redeeming once the new set is current. A new set is a credential change: this session is rotated and the account's other sessions are revoked. Needs a session at the default requirement, or a recovery-only one replacing a lost set.

post.summary: Recover the account with a saved code
post.description: Redeems one saved recovery code for a confirmed identifier. The session becomes recovery-only: it has no level, every other session of the account is revoked, and it may only set a password, enrol TOTP or make new codes. The account's confirmed address is told at once. The reply is the same for an unknown account, after the same argon2id work.
